sources.title: Evidence for an Electrifying Violation of Cosmic Censorship

evidence.text: Apply the DeTurck method with a planar Schwarzschild–AdS reference metric. Metric and gauge functions depend on two compact coordinates, with prescribed asymptotic data and regularity at the axis and horizon.

sources.title: Violating the Weak Cosmic Censorship Conjecture in Four-Dimensional Anti–de Sitter Space

evidence.text: Characteristic numerical evolution uses null geodesics angled by tan ψ=c/R, rather than boundary-normal characteristics, to cover an extremal horizon. Residual radial coordinate freedom keeps ξ=0 at an apparent horizon.

sources.title: Testing the Weak Gravity - Cosmic Censorship Connection

evidence.text: Continue fully nonlinear hairy solutions and, at fixed amplitude above amax, lower q while monitoring K=L⁴RabcdRabcd outside the horizon. Estimate the singular threshold qc by linear extrapolation of the inverse maximum curvature.

sources.title: Attempts at vacuum counterexamples to cosmic censorship in AdS

evidence.text: Branch continuation increases rotation amplitude while monitoring Cmax = maxM(CabcdCabcd). Fefferman–Graham expansions and holographic renormalization extract boundary stress tensors.

sources.title: Further evidence for the weak gravity — cosmic censorship connection

evidence.text: Numerical construction of static axisymmetric solutions uses the Einstein–DeTurck equations, a reference metric, and coordinates compactifying the Poincaré patch. Additional DeTurck-flow searches approached singular configurations rather than finding regular solutions beyond the reported boundaries; this is numerical evidence rather than an existence theorem.

sources.title: Weak cosmic censorship in Born–Infeld electrodynamics and bound on charge-to-mass ratio

evidence.text: Locate scalar zero modes by solving the time-independent scalar equation on fixed scalar-free backgrounds as an eigenvalue problem in q^2. Then solve the backreacted scalar system and monitor the maximal Kretschmann invariant and boundary condensate.

Can a reduced-phase-space, μ̄-scheme effective model describe both black-hole interior and exterior, resolve the Schwarzschild singularity, and determine the late-time geometry and its stability?
Can a vacuum bubble nucleated around a rotating AdS5 black hole support quasi-dS4 cosmology, and how do rotation, black-hole regularity and competing superradiance constrain nucleation and its rate?

Can a static, asymptotically flat regular black hole support a minimal FLRW daughter that expands without bound while remaining curvature regular, geodesically complete, and consistent with the averaged null energy condition?
